title: Mexico's Taekwondo Team Brings Home Four Medals from Dakar 2026 — the Sport's Best Youth Olympic Showing Ever
excerpt: Guillermo Cortés won silver and Aline Herrera, Jorge Octavio Martínez and the mixed team won bronze at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games, powering Mexico to a record 14 medals.
content:
Mexico's taekwondo team delivered the country's best Youth Olympic performance ever in Dakar, Senegal, winning four medals — one silver and three bronze — at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games, which closed Nov. 13.

Guillermo Cortés won silver in the men's -63 kg division, falling 2-1 in the final on Nov. 10 to Jordan's Abdallah Alzawahra, who became his country's first-ever Youth Olympic gold medalist. Alzawahra took the opening round 14-6, dropped the second 8-10, then won the deciding round 14-8.

Aline Sarai Herrera won bronze in the women's -55 kg division, where Senegal's Marie Sarr took gold on home soil and the United States' Karlee Vogel shared the bronze with Herrera. Jorge Octavio Martínez won bronze in the men's -73 kg division, after losing his semifinal to Jordan's Ahmad Al-Dahamsheh, who went on to beat Azerbaijan's Adil Kazimli 2-0 for the gold.

The fourth medal came in the mixed team event on Nov. 12 — the first time the event has awarded Olympic medals, after appearing as an exhibition at Tokyo 2020 and Paris 2024. The Mexican quartet of Cortés, Herrera, Martínez and Vania Mondragón lost its quarterfinal 0-2 to Türkiye, then fought back through the repechage, beating Saudi Arabia, and defeated Germany 2-1 in the bronze-medal match, taking the rounds 10-7, 30-37 and 24-10.

Jordan won the mixed team gold, beating Türkiye 2-0 in the final. The bronze made Cortés, Herrera and Martínez double medalists in Dakar, and gave Mondragón her first medal of the Games. Mexico was the only team from the Americas in the mixed team event.

It was the first time Mexico has won more than two taekwondo medals at a Youth Olympic Games. The country's previous bests were two medals each at Singapore 2010, Nanjing 2014 and Buenos Aires 2018.

The taekwondo medals were the final piece of a record haul for Mexico: the delegation finished Dakar 2026 with 14 medals — three silver and 11 bronze, no gold — the most Mexico has ever won at a Youth Olympic Games, topping the 12 medals from Buenos Aires 2018. Taekwondo contributed four of the 14, more than any other sport. The other silvers came from pole vaulter Carlo Cruz and beach wrestler Karen Ríos.

The Games ran Oct. 31 to Nov. 13 in Dakar, the first Olympic event ever held on the African continent, with 62 Mexican athletes competing.

Sources: CONADE / gob.mx, Nov. 2026; World Taekwondo, Nov. 2026; Frontera Informativa, Nov. 2026; Sendero Artes Marciales, Nov. 2026; The Jordan Today, Nov. 2026; Game On Field, Nov. 2026; Wikipedia, Taekwondo at the 2026 Summer Youth Olympics.
